chapters.title: All Wisdom Is from the Lord
chapters.html:
Sirach 1

1All wisdom is from the Lord,
and with Him it remains forever.

2The sand of the seas, the drops of rain,
and the days of eternity — who can count them?

3The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth,
the abyss, and wisdom — who can search them out?

4Wisdom was created before all things,
and prudent understanding from eternity.

5(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

6The root of wisdom — to whom has it been revealed?
Her subtle ways — who knows them?

7(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

8There is One who is wise, greatly to be feared,
seated upon His throne: the Lord.

9He Himself created her;
He saw her and numbered her,
and poured her out upon all His works.

10She is with all flesh according to His giving,
and He has supplied her to those who love Him.

11The fear of the Lord is glory and exultation,
and gladness and a crown of rejoicing.

12The fear of the Lord delights the heart,
and gives gladness and joy and long life.

13With him who fears the Lord it will go well at the end;
on the day of his death he will find favor.

14To fear God is the beginning of wisdom;
she was created with the faithful in the womb.

15She has made her nest among men, an everlasting foundation,
and among their descendants she will be trusted.

16To fear the Lord is the fullness of wisdom;
she makes men drunk with her fruits;

17she fills her whole house with desirable things,
and her storehouses with her produce.

18The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom,
making peace and perfect health flourish.

19He saw her and numbered her;
He rained down knowledge and discerning understanding,
and He exalted the glory of those who hold her fast.

20To fear the Lord is the root of wisdom,
and her branches are long life.

21(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

22Unrighteous anger cannot be justified,
for the sway of his anger is his downfall.

23A patient man will hold out until the right time,
and afterward joy will spring up for him.

24He will hide his words until the right time,
and the lips of the faithful will tell of his understanding.

25In the treasuries of wisdom are wise sayings,
but godliness is detestable to a sinner.

26If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments,
and the Lord will supply her to you.

27For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and discipline,
and faithfulness and meekness are His delight.

28Do not disobey the fear of the Lord,
and do not approach Him with a divided heart.

29Do not play the hypocrite before men,
and keep watch over your lips.

30Do not exalt yourself, or you may fall
and bring dishonor on yourself;
the Lord will reveal your secrets
and cast you down before the whole assembly,
because you did not come in the fear of the Lord,
and your heart was full of deceit.

Notes

  • v1 "All wisdom is from the Lord" — rendered from the Greek (Swete), the form in which the book was handed down; the author names himself in 50:27, Jesus son of Sirach of Jerusalem. Verse numbers follow the English.

  • vv5, 7, 21 — Swete's Greek gives these verse numbers and no words: some English Bibles have lines here from other copies. The numbers are kept so that the numbering matches, and the lines are left out.

  • v4 "Wisdom was created before all things" — the Greek of Proverbs 8:22 uses the same verb, The Lord created (ektisen) me as the beginning of His ways, where the Hebrew has got me.

  • vv14, 16, 18, 20 "the beginning… the fullness… the crown… the root of wisdom" — four sayings on the fear of the Lord, building on Proverbs 1:7 and 9:10.

  • v16 "she makes men drunk with her fruits" — methyskei: wisdom's feast, as in Proverbs 9:5, drink of the wine I have mixed.

  • v25 "godliness is detestable to a sinner" — bdelygma, as in Reproof 5:27 (Proverbs 29:27), one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.

  • v28 "with a divided heart" — kardia dissē, "a double heart": compare James 1:8, a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

chapters.title: Prepare Your Soul for Testing
chapters.html:
Sirach 2

1My child, if you come forward to serve the Lord God,
prepare your soul for testing.

2Set your heart straight and endure,
and do not be hasty in the time of calamity.

3Cling to Him and do not depart,
so that you may be increased at your end.

4Accept whatever is brought upon you,
and in the changes of your humiliation be patient.

5For gold is tested in the fire,
and acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation.

6Trust in Him, and He will help you;
make your ways straight, and hope in Him.

7You who fear the Lord, wait for His mercy,
and do not turn aside, or you may fall.

8You who fear the Lord, trust in Him,
and your reward will not fail.

9You who fear the Lord, hope for good things,
for everlasting gladness and mercy.

10Look at the generations of old and see:
who ever trusted in the Lord and was put to shame?
Or who ever remained in His fear and was forsaken?
Or who ever called upon Him, and He overlooked him?

11For the Lord is compassionate and merciful;
He forgives sins and saves in the time of affliction.

12Woe to timid hearts and slack hands,
and to the sinner who walks on two paths!

13Woe to the slack heart, for it does not trust;
therefore it will not be sheltered.

14Woe to you who have lost your endurance!
What will you do when the Lord visits you?

15Those who fear the Lord will not disobey His words,
and those who love Him will keep His ways.

16Those who fear the Lord will seek what pleases Him,
and those who love Him will be filled with the law.

17Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts,
and will humble their souls before Him.

18Let us fall into the hands of the Lord,
and not into the hands of men;
for as His majesty is,
so also is His mercy.

Notes

  • v1 "My child" — teknon, the teacher's word for his pupil, as "my son" is in Proverbs. "Testing" — peirasmos, trial or temptation: the one who comes to serve God should expect it.

  • v5 "gold is tested in the fire" — Proverbs 17:3 and Wisdom 3:6; Peter uses the picture of faith tested by fire (1 Peter 1:7).

  • vv7–9 "You who fear the Lord" — three times, and three more in vv15–17.

  • v10 "who ever trusted in the Lord and was put to shame?" — Psalm 22:4–5, in You they trusted and were not put to shame.

  • v11 "compassionate and merciful" — oiktirmōn kai eleēmōn, the words of the Greek of Exodus 34:6, God's own name proclaimed to Moses.

  • v12 "the sinner who walks on two paths" — compare Elijah: How long will you go limping between two opinions? (1 Kings 18:21).

  • v18 "Let us fall into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men" — David's choice in 2 Samuel 24:14, Let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great.

chapters.title: Honor Your Father
chapters.html:
Sirach 3

1Listen to me, your father, children,
and act accordingly, so that you may be saved.

2For the Lord has honored the father above his children,
and has established the right of the mother over her sons.

3Whoever honors his father atones for sins,

4and like one who lays up treasure
is he who glorifies his mother.

5Whoever honors his father will be gladdened by his own children,
and like one who lays up treasure
is he who glorifies his mother;
and on the day of his prayer he will be heard.

6Whoever glorifies his father will have long life,
and whoever listens to the Lord will give rest to his mother;

7he will serve his parents as his masters.

8Honor your father in deed and word,
so that a blessing may come upon you from him.

9For a father's blessing strengthens the houses of children,
but a mother's curse uproots their foundations.

10Do not glorify yourself in your father's dishonor,
for it is no glory to you.

11For a man's glory comes from his father's honor,
and a mother in disgrace is a reproach to her children.

12My child, help your father in his old age,
and do not grieve him as long as he lives;

13even if his understanding fails, be patient with him,
and do not despise him while you are in your full strength.

14For kindness shown to a father will not be forgotten,
and it will be built up for you against your sins;

15in the day of your affliction it will be remembered in your favor;
as fair weather on frost,
so your sins will melt away.

16Whoever forsakes his father is like a blasphemer,
and whoever angers his mother is cursed by the Lord.

17My child, carry out your work with meekness,
and you will be loved by worthy people.

18The greater you are, the more humble yourself,
and you will find favor before the Lord.

19(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

20For great is the power of the Lord,
and by the humble He is glorified.

21Do not seek what is too hard for you,
and do not search out what is too strong for you.

22Think about what has been commanded you,
for you have no need of what is hidden.

23Do not busy yourself with what is beyond your tasks,
for more than men can understand has been shown to you.

24For their own opinion has led many astray,
and wrong speculation has made their thoughts slip.

25(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

26Whoever loves danger will perish by it.
A stubborn heart will fare badly at the end;
a stubborn heart will be weighed down at the end.

27A stubborn heart will be weighed down with troubles,
and the sinner will heap sin upon sins.

28For the calamity of the proud there is no healing,
for a plant of wickedness has taken root in him.

29The heart of the intelligent will ponder a proverb,
and an attentive ear is the desire of the wise.

30Water will quench a blazing fire,
and charity atones for sins.

31Whoever repays favors is mindful of what lies ahead;
at the time of his fall he will find support.

Notes

  • vv1–16 — the commandment Honor your father and your mother (Exodus 20:12) taught at length: honoring parents is an offering to God (vv3, 14), and its reward is children, long life and answered prayer (vv5–6).

  • vv3, 14, 30 "atones for sins… built up for you against your sins… charity atones for sins" — exilasetai, the Greek word for the priests' atonement, used of a life of mercy. Proverbs says the same: By loyal love and truth iniquity is atoned for (16:6).

  • v5 — the Greek held here repeats the second line of v4 inside this verse; it is rendered as it stands.

  • vv19, 25 — Swete's Greek gives these verse numbers and no words (see the note on 1:5). The numbers are kept and the lines left out.

  • vv21–22 "Do not seek what is too hard for you… you have no need of what is hidden" — Psalm 131:1, I do not occupy myself with great matters; Deuteronomy 29:29, The hidden things belong to the LORD our God.

  • v26 — the Greek held here gives the "stubborn heart" line twice, with two verbs, and v27 takes it up a third time.

  • v30 "charity" — eleēmosynē, mercy shown in what is given, the "acts of charity" of Tobit (1:3; 4:10; 12:9). The same word is "kindness" in v14.

chapters.title: Do Not Cheat the Poor
chapters.html:
Sirach 4

1My child, do not cheat the poor of his living,
and do not keep needy eyes waiting.

2Do not grieve a hungry soul,
nor anger a man in his want.

3Do not add to the troubles of an angry heart,
nor delay your gift to one in need.

4Do not reject a suppliant in his distress,
nor turn your face away from the poor.

5Do not turn your eye away from the needy,
nor give a man cause to curse you;

6for if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul,
his Maker will hear his prayer.

7Make yourself loved in the assembly,
and bow your head to a great man.

8Incline your ear to the poor,
and answer him peaceably and with meekness.

9Rescue the wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer,
and do not be fainthearted in giving judgment.

10Be like a father to orphans,
and like a husband to their mother;
you will then be like a son of the Most High,
and He will love you more than your mother does.

11Wisdom exalts her sons,
and takes hold of those who seek her.

12Whoever loves her loves life,
and those who rise early for her will be filled with joy.

13Whoever holds her fast will inherit glory,
and wherever he goes, the Lord will bless.

14Those who serve her minister to the Holy One,
and the Lord loves those who love her.

15Whoever obeys her will judge the nations,
and whoever comes to her will dwell secure.

16If you trust her, you will inherit her,
and your descendants will keep possession of her.

17For at first she walks with him on winding ways;
she brings fear and dread upon him,
and torments him with her discipline
until she trusts his soul,
and tests him with her ordinances;

18then she comes straight back to him and gladdens him,
and reveals her secrets to him.

19If he goes astray, she will forsake him,
and hand him over to his own ruin.

20Watch for the right time, and beware of evil,
and do not be ashamed for your soul's sake;

21for there is a shame that brings sin,
and there is a shame that is glory and favor.

22Do not favor another at the cost of your own soul,
nor let respect for him bring you down.

23Do not hold back a word when it could save;

24for wisdom is known through speech,
and discipline through the words of the tongue.

25Do not speak against the truth,
but be ashamed of your lack of discipline.

26Do not be ashamed to confess your sins,
and do not try to force back the current of a river.

27Do not lay yourself down before a fool,
nor show partiality to a ruler.

28Fight to the death for the truth,
and the Lord God will fight for you.

29Do not be harsh with your tongue,
or sluggish and slack in your deeds.

30Do not be like a lion in your house,
nor capricious with your servants.

31Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive,
and closed when it is time to give back.

Notes

  • vv1–10 — the poor, the suppliant, the orphan and the widow: what the Law commands for them (Exodus 22:22–23; Deuteronomy 15:7–11) turned into counsel for one person.

  • v6 "his Maker will hear his prayer" — If you do afflict him — if he cries out to Me, I will surely hear his cry (Exodus 22:23).

  • v10 "you will then be like a son of the Most High" — Jesus: love your enemies, and do good… and you will be sons of the Most High (Luke 6:35).

  • v12 "those who rise early for her" — orthrizontes, as in Wisdom 6:14, "he who rises early for her."

  • v14 "minister to the Holy One" — leitourgēsousin hagiō, the words of priestly service: to serve wisdom is to serve God.

  • vv17–18 "at first she walks with him on winding ways… then she comes straight back to him" — wisdom tests her pupil before she trusts him, as discipline seems painful for the moment and later yields fruit (Hebrews 12:11). "Her discipline" — the Greek held here spells the word paidia, "play," for paideia, "discipline"; the context is discipline.

  • vv20–21 "a shame that brings sin… a shame that is glory" — the shame that keeps a man from what is right, and the shame that keeps him from what is wrong.

  • v26 "do not try to force back the current of a river" — confession is as natural as a river's flow; to hold it back is labor for nothing. Compare Proverbs 28:13 (Reproof 4:13).

  • v31 "stretched out to receive, and closed when it is time to give back" — compare Acts 20:35, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

chapters.title: Do Not Say, I Have Enough
chapters.html:
Sirach 5

1Do not rely on your wealth,
and do not say, "I have enough."

2Do not follow your own desire and strength,
walking in the lusts of your heart.

3Do not say, "Who will have power over me?"
for the Lord will surely punish you.

4Do not say, "I sinned, and what happened to me?"
for the Lord is patient.

5Do not be so sure of atonement
that you add sin to sins.

6Do not say, "His compassion is great;
He will atone for the multitude of my sins,"
for both mercy and wrath are with Him,
and His anger rests on sinners.

7Do not delay to turn to the Lord,
nor put it off from day to day;
for suddenly the wrath of the Lord will go forth,
and in the time of punishment you will perish.

8Do not rely on dishonest wealth,
for it will not help you in the day of calamity.

9Do not winnow with every wind,
nor walk on every path;
so does the double-tongued sinner.

10Stand firm in your understanding,
and let your word be one.

11Be quick to hear,
and give your answer with patience.

12If you have understanding, answer your neighbor;
if not, put your hand over your mouth.

13Glory and dishonor come from speaking,
and a man's tongue is his downfall.

14Do not be called a whisperer,
and do not lie in ambush with your tongue;
for shame comes upon the thief,
and harsh condemnation upon the double-tongued.

15In great things and in small, do not act in ignorance,

Notes

  • v1 "I have enough" — autarkē moi estin, the rich man's self-sufficiency; compare the rich fool, you have many goods laid up for many years (Luke 12:19).

  • vv4–7 "Do not say, 'I sinned, and what happened to me?'" — presuming on God's patience: Because the sentence against an evil deed is not carried out quickly, the heart of the children of man is fully set in them to do evil (Ecclesiastes 8:11). "Mercy and wrath are with Him" — both halves of God's name in Exodus 34:6–7.

  • v9 "Do not winnow with every wind" — turning with every breeze, as the double-tongued man says one thing here and another there (also v14 and 6:1).

  • v10 "let your word be one" — compare Matthew 5:37, Let your word be 'Yes, yes' or 'No, no'.

  • v11 "Be quick to hear" — tachys, the word of James 1:19, quick to hear, slow to speak.

  • v12 "put your hand over your mouth" — Job 40:4, I lay my hand on my mouth; Reproof 6:32 (Proverbs 30:32).

  • v15 — the sentence runs on into 6:1; the chapter break falls in the middle of it.

chapters.title: A Faithful Friend
chapters.html:
Sirach 6

1and do not become an enemy instead of a friend;
for a bad name inherits shame and reproach;
so does the double-tongued sinner.

2Do not exalt yourself in the plans of your soul,
or your soul will be torn in pieces like a bull;

3you will devour your leaves and destroy your fruit,
and will be left like a dry tree.

4An evil soul destroys the one who has it,
and makes him the laughingstock of his enemies.

5A sweet voice multiplies friends,
and a gracious tongue multiplies kind greetings.

6Let those who are at peace with you be many,
but let your counselors be one in a thousand.

7If you would gain a friend, gain him by testing him,
and do not be quick to trust him.

8For there is a friend when it suits him,
who will not stand by you in the day of your trouble.

9There is a friend who turns into an enemy,
and will bring a quarrel into the open to your shame.

10There is a friend who is a companion at table,
who will not stand by you in the day of your trouble.

11In your prosperity he will be like your own self,
and will speak boldly to your servants;

12but if you are brought low, he will turn against you,
and will hide himself from your presence.

13Keep yourself apart from your enemies,
and be on guard with your friends.

14A faithful friend is a strong shelter;
whoever has found one has found a treasure.

15Nothing can be given in exchange for a faithful friend,
and no scale can weigh his worth.

16A faithful friend is a medicine of life,
and those who fear the Lord will find him.

17Whoever fears the Lord directs his friendship rightly,
for as he is, so is his neighbor.

18My child, from your youth choose discipline,
and until your hair is gray you will keep finding wisdom.

19Come to her like one who plows and sows,
and wait for her good fruits;
for in working for her you will toil a little,
and soon you will eat of her produce.

20How very swift she is with the undisciplined!
The senseless man will not stay with her;

21she will lie on him like a heavy testing stone,
and he will not be slow to cast her off.

22For wisdom is like her name,
and she is not plain to many.

23Listen, my child, and accept my judgment,
and do not reject my counsel.

24Put your feet into her fetters,
and your neck into her collar.

25Put your shoulder under her and carry her,
and do not chafe at her bonds.

26Come to her with all your soul,
and keep her ways with all your might.

27Search out and seek, and she will become known to you;
and when you have hold of her, do not let her go.

28For at last you will find the rest she gives,
and she will be turned into joy for you.

29Then her fetters will become for you a strong shelter,
and her branches a glorious robe.

30For there is a golden ornament on her,
and her bonds are a cord of blue.

31You will put her on as a glorious robe,
and set her on your head as a crown of rejoicing.

32If you are willing, my child, you will be taught,
and if you give your soul to it, you will become shrewd.

33If you love to listen, you will gain knowledge,
and if you incline your ear, you will be wise.

34Stand in the company of the elders;
who is wise? Cling to him.

35Be willing to listen to every godly discourse,
and do not let wise proverbs escape you.

36If you see a man of understanding, rise early to go to him;
let your foot wear out his doorstep.

37Reflect on the statutes of the Lord,
and meditate on His commandments at all times.
It is He who will strengthen your heart,
and your desire for wisdom will be granted.

Notes

  • v2 "your soul will be torn in pieces like a bull" — the Greek line is obscure: pride tears a man apart as a bull is torn, and leaves him (v3) a dry tree with its leaves eaten.

  • vv5–17 — on friendship: the many and the one counselor (v6); a friend tested before he is trusted (v7); three false friends, for his own occasion, the turncoat, and the friend at table (vv8–12); the faithful friend (vv14–16). Compare Proverbs 18:24, there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

  • v16 "a medicine of life" — pharmakon zōēs: a friend who keeps one alive.

  • v18 "choose discipline" — the Greek held here spells it paidia, as in 4:17; the sense is paideia, "discipline."

  • v20 "How very swift she is with the undisciplined" — tacheia, "swift," as Swete prints it: wisdom is quickly gone from those who will not be taught. Tracheia, "rough," would differ by one letter.

  • v22 "wisdom is like her name" — the play on words behind this line does not show in the Greek; what is clear is the second half: she is not plain to many.

  • vv24–31 "fetters… collar… bonds… a cord of blue" — the marks of a slave become a robe and a crown. "A cord of blue" — klōsma hyakinthinon, the words of the Greek of Numbers 15:38, the blue cord on the tassels that reminded Israel of the commandments.

  • v29 "her branches" — kladoi, as Swete prints it; v24 has kloios, "collar," and the likeliest sense is that her collar becomes a glorious robe.

  • v37 "meditate on His commandments at all times" — Psalm 1:2, on His law he meditates day and night.

chapters.title: Remember Your End
chapters.html:
Sirach 7

1Do no evil, and evil will never overtake you.

2Stay away from wrong, and it will turn away from you.

3My son, do not sow in the furrows of injustice,
and you will not reap them sevenfold.

4Do not seek from the Lord the highest place,
nor from the king a seat of honor.

5Do not justify yourself before the Lord,
nor show off your wisdom before the king.

6Do not seek to become a judge,
if you are not strong enough to root out injustice;
or you may stand in awe of a powerful man,
and put a stumbling block in the way of your uprightness.

7Do not sin against the whole city,
nor disgrace yourself among the people.

8Do not repeat a sin,
for even for one you will not go unpunished.

9Do not say, "He will look upon the multitude of my gifts,
and when I make an offering to the Most High God,
He will accept it."

10Do not be fainthearted in your prayer,
and do not neglect to give charity.

11Do not laugh at a man who is bitter in soul,
for there is One who humbles and exalts.

12Do not devise a lie against your brother,
nor do the same to a friend.

13Do not be willing to tell any lie at all,
for the habit of it leads to no good.

14Do not babble in the company of elders,
and do not repeat your words in your prayer.

15Do not hate hard work,
or farming, which was created by the Most High.

16Do not count yourself among the crowd of sinners;
remember that wrath will not delay.

17Humble your soul greatly,
for the punishment of the ungodly is fire and worms.

18Do not exchange a friend for something of no account,
nor a true brother for the gold of Ophir.

19Do not let go of a wise and good wife,
for her grace is worth more than gold.

20Do not mistreat a servant who works faithfully,
nor a hired laborer who gives himself to his work.

21Let your soul love a good servant;
do not withhold his freedom from him.

22Do you have cattle? Look after them;
and if they are useful to you, keep them.

23Do you have children? Discipline them,
and bend their necks from their youth.

24Do you have daughters? Watch over their bodies,
and do not show them too cheerful a face.

25Give your daughter in marriage, and you will have finished a great work;
but give her to a man of understanding.

26Do you have a wife after your own heart? Do not divorce her.

27Honor your father with all your heart,
and do not forget your mother's birth pangs.

28Remember that through them you were born;
and what can you give back to them that equals what they gave you?

29With all your soul fear the Lord,
and revere His priests.

30With all your strength love your Maker,
and do not forsake His ministers.

31Fear the Lord and honor the priest,
and give him his portion, as you have been commanded from the beginning:
the offering for guilt, the gift of the shoulders,
the sacrifice of consecration, and the firstfruits.

32Stretch out your hand to the poor as well,
so that your blessing may be complete.

33A gift is welcome to all the living,
and do not withhold kindness from the dead.

34Do not fail those who weep,
and mourn with those who mourn.

35Do not hesitate to visit the sick,
for by such deeds you will be loved.

36In all your words remember your end,
and you will never sin.

Notes

  • v3 "do not sow in the furrows of injustice" — Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble (Proverbs 22:8); Job 4:8, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble reap it.

  • v8 "Do not repeat a sin" — literally "do not bind a sin twice."

  • v11 "there is One who humbles and exalts" — Hannah's song: He brings low; He also lifts up (1 Samuel 2:7).

  • v12 "Do not devise a lie" — literally "do not plow a lie," the Hebrew picture behind Proverbs 3:29, Do not plot harm against your neighbor, where the verb is "plow."

  • v14 "do not repeat your words in your prayer" — Jesus: When you pray, do not babble on as the Gentiles do, for they think they will be heard for their many words (Matthew 6:7).

  • v15 "farming, which was created by the Most High" — the work given to Adam in the garden and after it (Genesis 2:15; 3:23).

  • v17 "fire and worms" — the end of Isaiah (66:24), and Jesus, where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched (Mark 9:48).

  • v18 "the gold of Ophir" — the Greek has Soupheir, the land of fine gold (1 Kings 9:28; Job 28:16).

  • v21 "do not withhold his freedom from him" — the release of a Hebrew servant in the seventh year (Exodus 21:2; Deuteronomy 15:12).

  • vv27–31 "with all your heart… with all your soul… with all your strength" — the words of Deuteronomy 6:5 spread across father and mother, the Lord, and His priests. "The gift of the shoulders" — the priests' due from the sacrifices (Deuteronomy 18:3; Leviticus 7:32–34).

chapters.title: Whom Not to Quarrel With
chapters.html:
Sirach 8

1Do not contend with a powerful man,
or you may fall into his hands.

2Do not quarrel with a rich man,
or he may outweigh you;
for gold has destroyed many,
and has turned aside the hearts of kings.

3Do not fight with a loud-mouthed man,
and do not heap wood on his fire.

4Do not jest with an undisciplined man,
or your ancestors may be insulted.

5Do not reproach a man who is turning away from sin;
remember that we all deserve punishment.

6Do not dishonor a man in his old age,
for some of us are growing old.

7Do not rejoice over anyone's death;
remember that we all must die.

8Do not neglect the discourse of the wise,
but busy yourself with their proverbs;
for from them you will learn discipline,
and how to serve great men.

9Do not pass over the discourse of the aged,
for they themselves learned from their fathers;
from them you will learn understanding,
and how to give an answer in time of need.

10Do not kindle the coals of a sinner,
or you may be burned in his flaming fire.

11Do not get up and leave before an insolent man,
or he may lie in ambush for your words.

12Do not lend to a man stronger than you;
and if you do lend, count it as lost.

13Do not give surety beyond your means;
and if you give surety, be ready to pay.

14Do not go to law against a judge,
for they will decide in his favor because of his standing.

15Do not travel on the road with a reckless man,
or he may weigh you down;
for he will do as he pleases,
and through his folly you will perish with him.

16Do not quarrel with a hot-tempered man,
and do not cross the wilderness with him;
for blood is as nothing in his eyes,
and where there is no help, he will strike you down.

17Do not consult with a fool,
for he will not be able to keep a secret.

18Do not do a secret thing before a stranger,
for you do not know what it will give birth to.

19Do not open your heart to every man,
and do not let him repay you with a favor.

Notes

  • v2 "he may outweigh you" — antistēsē sou tēn holkēn, "set his weight against yours," the tipping of a scale: his money will outweigh your case.

  • v5 "we all deserve punishment" — en epitimois, "under rebuke": the one who has turned from sin should not be reminded of it by those who also need mercy.

  • vv8–9 "the discourse of the wise… of the aged" — for they themselves learned from their fathers: as Bildad says, ask, please, of the former generation (Job 8:8–10).

  • v13 "Do not give surety beyond your means" — Proverbs warns against surety altogether (6:1–5; 22:26–27); Sirach allows it within one's means, be ready to pay.

  • v16 "do not cross the wilderness with him" — where no one can come to your help.

  • v18 "what it will give birth to" — ti texetai: what the secret will lead to once a stranger knows it.

  • v19 "do not let him repay you with a favor" — the Greek line is obscure: perhaps a favor from one who knows your heart is a debt, or a hold over you.

chapters.title: An Old Friend Is Old Wine
chapters.html:
Sirach 9

1Do not be jealous of the wife you embrace,
and do not teach her an evil lesson to your own hurt.

2Do not give your soul to a woman,
so that she sets her foot on your strength.

3Do not go to meet a woman who plays the prostitute,
or you may fall into her snares.

4Do not keep company with a woman singer,
or you may be caught by her tricks.

5Do not gaze at a virgin,
or you may stumble and incur penalties for her.

6Do not give your soul to prostitutes,
or you may lose your inheritance.

7Do not look around in the streets of the city,
nor wander in its deserted places.

8Turn your eye away from a beautiful woman,
and do not gaze at beauty that belongs to another;
many have been led astray by a woman's beauty,
and by it desire is kindled like a fire.

9Never sit at table with a married woman,
nor drink wine with her at a feast,
or your heart may turn aside to her,
and in your spirit you slip into ruin.

10Do not forsake an old friend,
for a new one is not equal to him.
A new friend is new wine;
when it has grown old, you will drink it with joy.

11Do not envy the glory of a sinner,
for you do not know what his end will be.

12Do not delight in what pleases the ungodly;
remember that all the way to Hades they will not be held guiltless.

13Keep far from a man who has power to kill,
and you will not be troubled by the fear of death.
If you do approach him, make no mistake,
or he may take your life.
Know that you are walking among snares,
and strolling on the battlements of cities.

14As far as you can, take the measure of your neighbors,
and consult with the wise.

15Let your conversation be with men of understanding,
and let all your discussion be about the law of the Most High.

16Let righteous men be your companions at table,
and let your boast be in the fear of the Lord.

17A work is praised for the hand of its craftsmen,
and a leader of the people for the wisdom of his words.

18A loud-mouthed man is feared in his city,
and the man who is rash in speech will be hated.

Notes

  • vv1–9 — counsel about women, in the line of Proverbs 5–7: a jealous husband teaches his wife the very thing he fears (v1); the singer, the prostitute, another man's wife.

  • v5 "incur penalties for her" — the bride price and fine the Law lays on a man who seduces a virgin (Exodus 22:16–17; Deuteronomy 22:28–29).

  • v8 "do not gaze at beauty that belongs to another" — compare Matthew 5:28.

  • v10 "A new friend is new wine" — compare Luke 5:39, no one after drinking old wine wants new.

  • v13 "strolling on the battlements of cities" — on the top of the wall, in full view of every archer.

  • v15 "the law of the Most High" — nomos, as in 2:16.

  • v18 "A loud-mouthed man" — glōssōdēs, the word of 8:3.

chapters.title: Pride Was Not Created for Men
chapters.html:
Sirach 10

1A wise judge will discipline his people,
and the rule of a man of understanding will be well ordered.

2As the judge of a people is, so are his officials;
and as the ruler of a city is, so are all who live in it.

3An undisciplined king will ruin his people,
but a city will be built up by the understanding of its rulers.

4The government of the earth is in the hand of the Lord,
and over it He will raise up the right man for the time.

5A man's success is in the hand of the Lord,
and He will lay His honor upon the scribe.

6Do not be angry with your neighbor for every wrong,
and do nothing by acts of insolence.

7Arrogance is hateful before the Lord and before men,
and wrongdoing is an offense to both.

8Sovereignty passes from nation to nation
because of injustice and insolence and wealth.

9How can earth and ashes be proud?
For even while he lives I have cast out his inner parts.

10A long illness — the physician makes light of it;
today a king, and tomorrow he will die.

11For when a man dies,
he will inherit creeping things and wild beasts and worms.

12The beginning of a man's pride is to depart from the Lord;
his heart has turned away from his Maker.

13For the beginning of pride is sin,
and the man who clings to it will pour out detestable things.
Therefore the Lord brought unheard-of calamities on them,
and overthrew them utterly.

14The Lord has cast down the thrones of rulers,
and seated the meek in their place.

15The Lord has plucked up the roots of nations,
and planted the humble in their place.

16The Lord has overthrown the lands of nations,
and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.

17He has withered some of them and destroyed them,
and made the memory of them cease from the earth.

18Pride was not created for men,
nor fierce anger for those born of women.

19What seed is held in honor? The seed of man.
What seed is held in honor? Those who fear the Lord.
What seed is held in dishonor? The seed of man.
What seed is held in dishonor? Those who break the commandments.

20Among brothers their leader is honored,
and those who fear the Lord are honored in His eyes.

21(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

22The rich, the noble and the poor —
their glory is the fear of the Lord.

23It is not right to dishonor a poor man who has understanding,
nor is it fitting to honor a sinful man.

24The great man, the judge and the ruler will be honored,
but none of them is greater than the one who fears the Lord.

25Free men will serve a wise servant,

  • v10 "the physician makes light of it" — skōptei, "jests": the line is obscure; it may mean that a long illness is made light of until the king who has it dies.

  • v11 "creeping things and wild beasts and worms" — compare Isaiah 14:11, worms are your covering.

  • vv14–17 "The Lord has cast down the thrones of rulers, and seated the meek in their place" — Mary's song uses the same verb, He has brought down (kathelen) the mighty from their thrones and lifted up the humble (Luke 1:52); Hannah's song before it, He raises the poor from the dust… to seat them with nobles (1 Samuel 2:8).

chapters.title: Call No One Blessed Before His Death
chapters.html:
Sirach 11

1The wisdom of a humble man will lift up his head,
and seat him among great men.

2Do not praise a man for his good looks,
nor abhor a man for his appearance.

3The bee is small among flying creatures,
but what she makes is the best of sweet things.

4Do not boast of the clothes you wear,
nor exalt yourself on the day of honor;
for the works of the Lord are wonderful,
and His works are hidden from men.

5Many monarchs have sat on the ground,
and one never thought of has worn the crown.

6Many rulers have been greatly disgraced,
and the honored have been handed over to others.

7Do not find fault before you investigate;
first consider, and then rebuke.

8Do not answer before you have heard,
and do not interrupt in the middle of what is said.

9Do not argue about a matter that does not concern you,
and do not sit with sinners when they judge.

10My child, do not busy yourself with many matters;
if you multiply them, you will not go unpunished;
if you pursue, you will not overtake,
and by running away you will not escape.

11There is one who works and toils and hurries,
and is all the more behind.

12There is another who is slow and needs help,
lacking in strength and abounding in poverty;
but the eyes of the Lord look upon him for good,
and He lifts him up from his low estate,

13and raises his head,
and many are amazed at him.

14Good things and bad, life and death,
poverty and wealth, come from the Lord.

15(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

16(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

17The gift of the Lord remains with the godly,
and His good pleasure brings lasting success.

18There is a man who grows rich by his care and his stinginess,
and this is the portion of his reward:

19when he says, "I have found rest,
and now I will eat of my goods,"
he does not know how much time will pass
until he leaves them to others and dies.

20Stand by your covenant and give yourself to it,
and grow old in your work.

21Do not marvel at the works of a sinner,
but trust in the Lord and keep at your work;
for it is easy in the sight of the Lord
to make a poor man rich quickly, in a moment.

22The blessing of the Lord is the reward of the godly,
and quickly He makes His blessing flourish.

23Do not say, "What do I need?
What good things will be mine from now on?"

24Do not say, "I have enough,
and what harm can come to me from now on?"

25In the day of prosperity, adversity is forgotten,
and in the day of adversity, prosperity is not remembered.

26For it is easy for the Lord on the day of death
to repay a man according to his ways.

27An hour's misfortune makes one forget delights,
and at a man's end his deeds are revealed.

28Call no one blessed before his death;
a man will be known by his children.

29Do not bring every man into your house,
for many are the snares of the deceitful.

30Like a decoy partridge in a cage,
so is the heart of a proud man,
and like a spy he watches for your fall;

31for he lies in wait, turning good into evil,
and on things worthy of praise he will put blame.

32From a spark of fire comes a heap of coals,
and a sinful man lies in wait for blood.

33Beware of a scoundrel, for he plans evil,
or he may give you a lasting blemish.

34Take a stranger into your home,
and he will upset you with troubles,
and make you a stranger to your own.

Notes

  • vv5–6 "Many monarchs have sat on the ground, and one never thought of has worn the crown" — compare Hannah's song, He raises the poor from the dust… to seat them with nobles (1 Samuel 2:8). "Monarchs" — tyrannoi, as in Wisdom 6:9.

  • v8 "Do not answer before you have heard" — Proverbs 18:13, If one gives an answer before he hears, it is his folly and shame.

  • v14 "Good things and bad… come from the Lord" — Job 2:10, Shall we receive good from God, and not receive evil?

  • vv15–16 — Swete's Greek gives these verse numbers and no words (see the note on 1:5).

  • vv18–19 "I have found rest, and now I will eat of my goods" — the rich fool of Jesus' parable says the same, and dies that night (Luke 12:16–21).

  • v20 "Stand by your covenant" — diathēkē: here the task or agreement a man has taken on; keep at it until old age.

  • v22 "The blessing of the Lord is the reward of the godly" — compare Proverbs 10:22, The blessing of the LORD makes rich.

  • v24 "I have enough" — the words of 5:1.

  • v30 "a decoy partridge in a cage" — a tame bird set out to lure wild ones into the trap; the proud man's heart is bait.

  • v33 "a lasting blemish" — mōmos, a blemish or blame that stays on a man's name.

chapters.title: Know to Whom You Do Good
chapters.html:
Sirach 12

1If you do a kindness, know to whom you do it,
and you will be thanked for your good deeds.

2Do good to a godly man, and you will be repaid —
if not by him, then by the Most High.

3No good comes to one who persists in evil,
or to one who does not give charity.

4Give to the godly man,
but do not help the sinner.

5Do good to the humble, but do not give to the ungodly;
hold back his bread and do not give it to him,
or by it he may overpower you;
for you will receive twice as much evil
for all the good you do him.

6For the Most High also hates sinners,
and will repay the ungodly with punishment.

7Give to the good man,
but do not help the sinner.

8A friend is not proved in prosperity,
and an enemy will not stay hidden in adversity.

9When a man prospers, his enemies are grieved,
and in his adversity even his friend will part from him.

10Never trust your enemy,
for as bronze corrodes, so does his wickedness.

11Even if he humbles himself and goes about bowed down,
take heed to yourself and be on guard against him;
you will be to him like one who has polished a mirror,
and you will know that his rust has not been wiped away for good.

12Do not stand him beside you,
or he may overturn you and take your place;
do not seat him at your right hand,
or he may seek your seat,
and in the end you will understand my words,
and be stung by what I said.

13Who will pity a snake charmer who is bitten,
or anyone who goes near wild beasts?

14So no one will pity a man who keeps company with a sinner
and becomes caught up in his sins.

15He will stay with you for a while,
but if you falter, he will not stand by you.

16An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips,
but in his heart he plans to throw you into a pit;
an enemy will weep with his eyes,
but if he finds an opportunity, he will never have his fill of blood.

17If misfortune meets you, you will find him there before you,
and while seeming to help, he will trip your heel.

18He will shake his head and clap his hands,
and whisper much, and change his expression.

Notes

  • vv4–7 "do not give to the ungodly; hold back his bread" — counsel of caution, and hard beside Reproof 1:21 (Proverbs 25:21), If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat, which Paul quotes (Romans 12:20), and Jesus' love your enemies, and do good (Luke 6:35). Sirach speaks of feeding a man who will use the gift against you; the Proverb, of answering hatred with bread.

  • v8 "A friend is not proved in prosperity" — ouk ekdikēthēsetai, "will not be vindicated": good times do not show who is a true friend; bad times show who is an enemy.

  • vv10–11 "as bronze corrodes… like one who has polished a mirror" — mirrors were of bronze: wiping one clears it for a moment, but the tarnish returns. The enemy's humility is a polish.

  • v13 "a snake charmer who is bitten" — as in Ecclesiastes 10:11, there is no gain for the charmer when the snake bites first.

  • v16 "An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips" — Psalm 55:21, His speech was smoother than butter, but war was in his heart.

  • v17 "he will trip your heel" — compare Psalm 41:9, who ate my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.

  • v18 "He will shake his head and clap his hands" — the gestures of mockery at another's ruin (Lamentations 2:15).

chapters.title: The Rich and the Poor
chapters.html:
Sirach 13

1Whoever touches pitch will be defiled,
and whoever keeps company with a proud man will become like him.

2Do not lift a weight beyond your strength,
and do not keep company with one stronger and richer than you.
What has the clay pot in common with the kettle?
The one will strike against it, and the pot will be smashed.

3A rich man does wrong, and he himself snorts with indignation;
a poor man is wronged, and he himself must beg pardon.

4If you are of use to him, he will work you;
and if you are in need, he will forsake you.

5If you have something, he will live with you and drain you dry,
and he himself will feel no pain.

6When he needs you, he will deceive you,
and smile at you and give you hope;
he will speak kindly to you and say, "What do you need?"

7He will shame you with his food,
until he has drained you two or three times,
and at last he will mock you.
Afterward, when he sees you, he will pass you by,
and shake his head at you.

8Take care not to be led astray,
and not to be humbled in your merrymaking.

9When a powerful man invites you, hold back,
and he will invite you all the more.

10Do not push forward, or you may be pushed away;
and do not stand too far off, or you may be forgotten.

11Do not presume to speak with him as an equal,
nor trust his many words;
for by much talk he will test you,
and while smiling he will examine you.

12Merciless is he who does not keep your words to himself;
he will not spare you harm or chains.

13Keep them to yourself and be very careful,
for you are walking with your own downfall.

14(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

15Every creature loves its like,
and every man his neighbor;

16all flesh gathers by kind,
and a man clings to one like himself.

17What fellowship has a wolf with a lamb?
No more has a sinner with the godly.

18What peace is there between a hyena and a dog?
What peace between the rich and the poor?

19Wild donkeys in the wilderness are the prey of lions;
so the poor are the pasture of the rich.

20Humility is detestable to a proud man;
so a poor man is detestable to a rich one.

21When a rich man totters, he is held up by his friends,
but when a humble man falls, he is pushed away by his friends as well.

22When a rich man slips, many come to his aid;
he says what should not be said, and they justify him.
A humble man slips, and they rebuke him besides;
he speaks sense, and no place is given him.

23The rich man speaks, and all are silent,
and they extol his word to the clouds;
the poor man speaks, and they say, "Who is this?"
and if he stumbles, they push him down.

24Riches are good if there is no sin in them,
and poverty is evil in the mouth of the godly.

25A man's heart changes his face,
whether for good or for evil.

26The sign of a heart in good spirits is a cheerful face,
but the devising of proverbs is wearisome thinking.

Notes

  • v2 "the clay pot… the kettle" — earthenware against bronze: when they meet, only one breaks.

  • vv3–7 — how a rich man uses a poor one: he works him, drains him, feeds him to shame him, and shakes his head at him.

  • vv9–10 "When a powerful man invites you, hold back, and he will invite you all the more" — compare Jesus' counsel to take the lowest place at a feast (Luke 14:8–10).

  • v14 — Swete's Greek gives this verse number and no words (see the note on 1:5).

  • v17 "What fellowship has a wolf with a lamb?" — compare Paul, what fellowship has light with darkness? (2 Corinthians 6:14); only in the age to come will the wolf dwell with the lamb (Isaiah 11:6).

  • v21 "When a rich man totters, he is held up by his friends" — Proverbs 19:4, Wealth adds many friends, but the poor man is separated from his friend.

  • v23 "the poor man speaks, and they say, 'Who is this?'" — as in Ecclesiastes 9:16, the poor man's wisdom is despised and his words are not heard.

  • v24 "poverty is evil in the mouth of the godly" — eusebous, "godly," as Swete prints it: even the godly call poverty an evil. The line reads more easily with asebous, "ungodly."

  • v26 "the devising of proverbs is wearisome thinking" — compare Ecclesiastes 12:12, much study is a weariness of the flesh.

chapters.title: The Decree of Death
chapters.html:
Sirach 14

1Blessed is the man who has not slipped with his mouth,
and is not stung by grief for sin;

2blessed is he whose soul does not condemn him,
and who has not fallen from his hope.

3Riches are not fitting for a stingy man,
and what use is money to a grudging man?

4Whoever gathers by depriving himself gathers for others,
and others will live in luxury on his goods.

5If a man is mean to himself, to whom will he be good?
He will not enjoy his own riches.

6No one is meaner than the man who is grudging to himself,
and this is the reward of his wickedness;

7even if he does good, he does it by forgetfulness,
and in the end he shows his wickedness.

8Evil is the man with a grudging eye;
he turns away his face and disregards souls.

9The eye of the greedy man is not satisfied with his portion,
and wicked injustice withers the soul.

10An evil eye begrudges bread,
and there is nothing on his own table.

11My child, treat yourself well according to your means,
and bring offerings to the Lord as is fitting.

12Remember that death will not delay,
and the decree of Hades has not been shown to you.

13Before you die, do good to a friend,
and as far as you are able, reach out and give to him.

14Do not deprive yourself of a good day;
do not let your share of good desire pass you by.

15Will you not leave the fruit of your labors to another,
and what you toiled for to be divided by lot?

16Give and take, and treat yourself well,
for in Hades one cannot look for luxury.

17All flesh grows old like a garment,
for the decree from of old is, "Dying you shall die."

18Like leaves growing on a thick tree,
which sheds some and grows others,
so are the generations of flesh and blood:
one comes to an end, and another is born.

19Every work decays and comes to an end,
and the one who made it will go with it.

20Blessed is the man who will end his days in wisdom,
and who reasons with his understanding;

21who ponders her ways in his heart,
and will come to understand her secrets.

22Go after her like a hunter,
and lie in wait at her entrances.

23He who peers through her windows
will also listen at her doors;

24he who lodges close to her house
will also fasten a tent peg in her walls;

25he will pitch his tent beside her,
and lodge in a good lodging place;

26he will set his children under her shelter,
and will dwell under her branches;

27he will be sheltered by her from the heat,
and will lodge in her glory.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Blessed is the man… whose soul does not condemn him" — compare 1 John 3:21, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God.

  • vv3–10 "a grudging man… a grudging eye" — baskanos, the evil eye that begrudges: Proverbs 23:6, Do not eat the bread of a stingy man; Jesus, is your eye evil because I am good? (Matthew 20:15).

  • v9 "The eye of the greedy man is not satisfied" — Ecclesiastes 4:8, his eyes are never satisfied with riches.

  • v12 "the decree of Hades" — diathēkē, "covenant" or "decree": the appointed terms of death, which no one is shown in advance.

  • vv14–16 "Give and take, and treat yourself well, for in Hades one cannot look for luxury" — Ecclesiastes 2:18–21 and 9:10, there is no work… in Sheol. "Treat yourself well" — apatēson tēn psychēn sou, literally "beguile your soul," that is, give it its pleasure.

  • v17 "Dying you shall die" — thanatō apothanē, the words of the Greek of Genesis 2:17, the first decree, rendered here as Genesis has them. "Like a garment" — Psalm 102:26, they will all wear out like a garment.

  • v20 "who will end his days in wisdom" — teleutēsei, "will die," as Swete prints it; the parallel lines (vv20–21) speak of reasoning and pondering, and "meditate" would fit them more closely.

  • vv22–27 — the seeker of wisdom pictured as a lover: he peers through her windows (compare Song of Songs 2:9, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice), pitches his tent against her walls, and raises his children in her shade.

chapters.title: Fire and Water
chapters.html:
Sirach 15

1Whoever fears the Lord will do this,
and whoever holds fast to the law will gain her.

2She will come to meet him like a mother,
and welcome him like the bride of his youth.

3She will feed him with the bread of understanding,
and give him the water of wisdom to drink.

4He will lean on her and not fall;
he will rely on her and not be put to shame.

5She will exalt him above his neighbors,
and among the assembly she will open his mouth.

6He will inherit gladness and a crown of rejoicing,
and an everlasting name.

7Foolish men will not attain her,
and sinners will not see her.

8She is far from pride,
and liars will never remember her.

9Praise is not fitting in the mouth of a sinner,
for it has not been sent from the Lord.

10For praise is spoken in wisdom,
and the Lord will prosper it.

11Do not say, "Because of the Lord I fell away";
what He hates, you must not do.

12Do not say, "It was He who led me astray,"
for He has no need of a sinful man.

13The Lord hates every detestable thing,
and it is not loved by those who fear Him.

14It was He who made man in the beginning,
and He left him in the power of his own counsel.

15If you are willing, you will keep the commandments,
and to keep faith is for you to choose.

16He has set before you fire and water;
stretch out your hand to whichever you wish.

17Before man are life and death,
and whichever he chooses will be given him.

18For great is the wisdom of the Lord;
He is mighty in power and sees all things;

19His eyes are on those who fear Him,
and He knows every work of man.

20He has commanded no one to be ungodly,
and He has given no one license to sin.

Notes

  • vv2–3 "like a mother… like the bride of his youth… the bread of understanding… the water of wisdom" — wisdom keeps her house and sets her table, as in Proverbs 9:1–5; Jesus speaks of the bread of life and the living water (John 4:10; 6:35).

  • v5 "among the assembly she will open his mouth" — en mesō ekklēsias, the words of the Greek of Psalm 22:22, among the congregation I will praise You.

  • vv11–13 "Do not say, 'It was He who led me astray'" — no one may blame God for his sin: Let no one say when he is tempted, "I am being tempted by God" (James 1:13). "What He hates, you must not do" — so Swete's Greek (ou poiēseis, "you will not do").

  • v14 "He left him in the power of his own counsel" — diaboulion, a man's own deliberation and choice: God made man able to choose.

  • vv16–17 "fire and water… life and death" — Moses' last charge: I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life (Deuteronomy 30:19).

  • v20 "He has given no one license to sin" — anesis, "relief, leave": God's patience is not permission.

chapters.title: Mercy and Wrath Are with Him
chapters.html:
Sirach 16

1Do not desire a multitude of worthless children,
nor rejoice in ungodly sons.

2If they multiply, do not rejoice in them,
unless the fear of the Lord is with them.

3Do not trust in their life,
and do not rely on their standing;
for one is better than a thousand,
and to die childless is better than to have ungodly children.

4For through one man of understanding a city will be peopled,
but a tribe of lawless men will be laid waste.

5Many such things my eyes have seen,
and my ear has heard things stronger than these.

6In an assembly of sinners a fire will be kindled,
and against a disobedient nation wrath has blazed up.

7He did not forgive the giants of old,
who rebelled in their strength.

8He did not spare the neighbors among whom Lot lived as a guest,
whom He abhorred for their pride.

9He showed no pity to a nation doomed to destruction,
who were taken away in their sins;

10so it was with the six hundred thousand on foot
who gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.

11Even if there is only one stiff-necked man,
it would be a wonder if he went unpunished.
For mercy and wrath are with Him;
He is mighty to forgive, and He pours out wrath.

12As great as His mercy, so great also is His reproof;
He judges a man according to his works.

13The sinner will not escape with his plunder,
and the patience of the godly will not go unrewarded.

14He will make room for every act of charity;
each will find according to his works.

15(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

16(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

17Do not say, "I will hide from the Lord;
who from on high will remember me?
Among so many people I will not be noticed;
for what is my soul in a boundless creation?

18The heaven, and the highest heaven of God,
the abyss and the earth will shake when He visits them;

19the mountains and the foundations of the earth together
tremble and quake when He looks upon them;

20but no heart will think about these things,
and who will consider His ways?

21There is a storm that no man will see,
and most of His works are hidden.

22Who will announce works of justice?
Or who will wait for them? For the covenant is far off."

23These are the thoughts of one who lacks understanding;
a foolish man who has gone astray thinks foolish things.

24Listen to me, my child, and gain knowledge,
and set your heart on my words.

25I will set out discipline by weight,
and declare knowledge with precision.

26When the Lord made His works in the beginning by His judgment,
from their making He set apart their portions.

27He set His works in order forever,
and their dominions for their generations;
they neither hunger nor grow weary,
and they do not leave off from their tasks.

28None of them crowds its neighbor,
and they never disobey His word.

29After this the Lord looked upon the earth,
and filled it with His good things.

30With every kind of living thing He covered its face,
and into it they return.

Notes

  • v3 "one is better than a thousand" — one righteous child outweighs a crowd of ungodly ones.

  • v6 "In an assembly of sinners a fire will be kindled" — as fire came out from the LORD on Korah's company (Numbers 16:35; Psalm 106:18, Fire blazed among their company).

  • vv7–10 — four examples: the giants before the Flood (Genesis 6:4; Wisdom 14:6); Sodom, where Lot lived as a guest (Genesis 19), abhorred for their pride; the nations of Canaan; and the six hundred thousand on foot who came out of Egypt and died in the wilderness (Numbers 11:21; 14:22–35).

  • v11 "mercy and wrath are with Him" — the words of 5:6.

  • v12 "He judges a man according to his works" — Psalm 62:12, You repay a man according to his work; Romans 2:6.

  • vv15–16 — Swete's Greek gives these verse numbers and no words (see the note on 1:5).

  • vv17–22 — the doubter's own words: God is too high to notice one soul, and His judgment too far off to fear. "The covenant is far off" — diathēkē, the decree of judgment, as in 14:12. Verse 23 answers him.

  • v18 "the heaven, and the highest heaven of God" — as Solomon prayed, The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You (1 Kings 8:27).

  • vv26–30 — the order of creation in Genesis 1: the lights in their courses, then the earth filled and its living things, who return to it (Psalm 104:29).

chapters.title: Man from the Earth
chapters.html:
Sirach 17

1The Lord created man out of earth,
and turned him back to it again.

2He gave them a fixed number of days and a time,
and gave them authority over the things on the earth.

3He clothed them with strength fit for them,
and made them in His own image.

4He put the fear of them upon all flesh,
and gave them dominion over beasts and birds.

5(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

6Counsel and tongue and eyes,
ears and a heart for thinking, He gave them.

7He filled them with knowledge and understanding,
and showed them good and evil.

8He set His eye upon their hearts,
to show them the majesty of His works,

9so that they might tell of the majesty of His works,

10and praise His holy name.

11He gave them knowledge besides,
and gave them the law of life as an inheritance.

12He established an everlasting covenant with them,
and showed them His judgments.

13Their eyes saw the majesty of His glory,
and their ears heard the glory of their voice.

14He said to them, "Beware of all unrighteousness,"
and He gave each of them a command concerning his neighbor.

15Their ways are always before Him;
they will not be hidden from His eyes.

16(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

17For every nation He appointed a ruler,
but Israel is the Lord's portion.

18(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

19All their works are as clear as the sun before Him,
and His eyes are always on their ways.

20Their iniquities are not hidden from Him,
and all their sins are before the Lord.

21(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

22A man's charity is like a signet ring with Him,
and He will keep a man's kindness like the apple of His eye.

23Afterward He will rise up and repay them,
and bring their recompense on their own heads.

24Yet to those who repent He grants a way back,
and He encourages those whose endurance is failing.

25Turn back to the Lord and forsake your sins;
pray before His face and lessen your offense.

26Return to the Most High and turn away from iniquity,
and utterly hate what is detestable.

27Who will sing praise to the Most High in Hades,
in place of the living who give thanks?

28From the dead, as from one who does not exist, thanksgiving has ceased;
he who is alive and well will praise the Lord.

29How great is the mercy of the Lord,
and His forgiveness for those who turn to Him!

30For not everything is possible for men,
since a son of man is not immortal.

31What is brighter than the sun? Yet it fails;
and an evil man will set his mind on flesh and blood.

32He watches over the host of the heights of heaven,
but all men are earth and ashes.

Notes

  • vv1–14 — creation and the giving of the law told as one story: man from the earth (Genesis 2:7; 3:19), in God's image (1:27), knowing good and evil (2:17), then the covenant and the law at Sinai, where their eyes saw and their ears heard (Deuteronomy 4:12, 36; 5:24).

  • v4 "He put the fear of them upon all flesh" — Genesis 9:2, The fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every living thing of the earth.

  • vv5, 16, 18, 21 — Swete's Greek gives these verse numbers and no words (see the note on 1:5).

  • v13 "the glory of their voice" — so Swete's Greek (phōnēs autōn); the voice heard at Sinai was God's, and "His voice" is what the line means.

  • v14 "a command concerning his neighbor" — You shall be sure to correct your neighbor… you shall love your neighbor as yourself (Leviticus 19:17–18).

  • v17 "For every nation He appointed a ruler, but Israel is the Lord's portion" — Deuteronomy 32:8–9: the Greek there has the nations bounded according to the number of the angels of God, and the LORD's portion is His people.

  • v22 "like a signet ring… like the apple of His eye" — kept close as a seal is worn (Haggai 2:23), and guarded as the pupil of His eye (Deuteronomy 32:10).

  • vv27–28 "Who will sing praise to the Most High in Hades?" — Psalm 6:5, in Sheol who will praise You?; Isaiah 38:18–19, the living, the living, he thanks You.

  • v30 "a son of man" — huios anthrōpou, a human being, as in Psalm 8:4, what is man… and the son of man.

  • v32 "earth and ashes" — the words of 10:9 and of Abraham in Genesis 18:27.

chapters.title: What Is Man?
chapters.html:
Sirach 18

1He who lives forever created the whole universe together;

2the Lord alone will be declared righteous.

3(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

4To no one has He given power to proclaim His works;
and who can search out His mighty deeds?

5Who can measure the might of His majesty?
Who can go on to recount His mercies?

6It is not possible to take from them or add to them,
nor is it possible to search out the wonders of the Lord.

7When a man has finished, then he is only beginning;
and when he stops, he is left at a loss.

8What is man, and of what use is he?
What is his good, and what is his evil?

9The number of a man's days is great if it reaches a hundred years.

10Like a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand,
so are a few years in the day of eternity.

11Therefore the Lord is patient with them,
and pours out His mercy upon them.

12He sees and recognizes that their end is evil;
therefore He has multiplied His forgiveness.

13The mercy of a man is for his neighbor,
but the mercy of the Lord is for all flesh.
He rebukes and disciplines and teaches,
and brings them back as a shepherd his flock.

14He has mercy on those who accept discipline,
and who are eager for His judgments.

15My child, do not mix blame with your good deeds,
nor bring grief by your words with any gift you give.

16Does not the dew relieve the scorching heat?
So a word is better than a gift.

17Is not a word better than a good gift?
Both are found in a gracious man.

18A fool will reproach ungraciously,
and the gift of a grudging man makes the eyes waste away.

19Learn before you speak,
and take care of your health before you fall sick.

20Before judgment, examine yourself,
and in the hour of visitation you will find forgiveness.

21Before you fall ill, humble yourself,
and when you have sinned, show that you have turned back.

22Let nothing hinder you from paying a vow in good time,
and do not wait until death to be set right.

23Before you make a vow, prepare yourself,
and do not be like a man who tests the Lord.

24Think of His wrath in the days of your end,
and of the time of vengeance, when He turns away His face.

25In the time of plenty, think of the time of hunger;
in the days of wealth, think of poverty and want.

26From morning to evening the time changes,
and all things move swiftly before the Lord.

27A wise man is cautious in everything,
and in days of sin he guards against wrongdoing.

28Every intelligent man knows wisdom,
and he gives thanks to the one who has found her.

29Those who are intelligent in words have also become wise themselves,
and have poured out exact proverbs.

30Self-control of the soul.
Do not follow your desires,
but hold back from your appetites.

31If you grant your soul what its desire pleases,
it will make you the laughingstock of your enemies.

32Do not delight in much luxury,
nor be tied to the cost of it.

33Do not become a beggar by feasting on borrowed money,
when there is nothing in your purse.

Notes

  • v3 — Swete's Greek gives this verse number and no words (see the note on 1:5).

  • v8 "What is man, and of what use is he?" — compare Psalm 8:4, what is man, that You remember him, and Job 7:17.

  • vv9–10 "a hundred years… a drop of water from the sea" — set against eternity, even a long life is a drop; Psalm 90:10 gives seventy or eighty years.

  • v13 "as a shepherd his flock" — Isaiah 40:11, He will feed His flock like a shepherd. A man's mercy reaches his neighbor; God's reaches all flesh.

  • v17 "a gracious man" — kecharitōmenos, "one who has been graced," the word the messenger uses to greet Mary (Luke 1:28, kecharitōmenē).

  • v20 "Before judgment, examine yourself" — compare Paul, let a man examine himself (1 Corinthians 11:28).

  • vv22–23 "paying a vow in good time… do not be like a man who tests the Lord" — Ecclesiastes 5:4, When you make a vow to God, do not delay to pay it; Deuteronomy 6:16, You shall not test the LORD your God.

  • v30 "Self-control of the soul." — a heading written into the Greek text itself, over the sayings that follow; another stands at 20:26.

chapters.title: Let It Die with You
chapters.html:
Sirach 19

1A worker who is a drunkard will not become rich;
whoever despises small things will fall little by little.

2Wine and women lead men of understanding astray,
and whoever clings to prostitutes grows reckless.

3Decay and worms will inherit him,
and the reckless soul will be cut off.

4Whoever trusts too quickly is light-headed,
and whoever sins wrongs his own soul.

5Whoever takes delight in his heart will be condemned,

6and whoever hates gossip has less evil.

7Never repeat what is said,
and you will lose nothing at all.

8Do not tell it to friend or foe,
and unless it would be a sin for you, do not reveal it;

9for he has heard you and will watch you,
and when the time comes he will hate you.

10Have you heard something? Let it die with you.
Take heart: it will not make you burst.

11Because of one word a fool goes into labor,
like a woman giving birth to a child.

12Like an arrow stuck in the flesh of the thigh,
so is a word inside a fool.

13Question a friend; perhaps he did not do it;
and if he did anything, so that he may not do it again.

14Question your friend; perhaps he did not say it;
and if he said it, so that he may not say it again.

15Question a friend, for often it is slander,
and do not believe everything you hear.

16A man may slip without meaning it;
and who has not sinned with his tongue?

17Question your neighbor before you threaten him,
and give the law of the Most High its place.

18(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

19(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

20All wisdom is the fear of the Lord,
and in all wisdom there is the doing of the law.

21(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

22The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom,
nor is there prudence where sinners take counsel.

23There is a wickedness that is detestable,
and there is a fool who merely lacks wisdom.

24Better is the God-fearing man who has little understanding
than one rich in intelligence who breaks the law.

25There is a cleverness that is exact and unjust,
and there is one who twists a kindness to win a verdict.

26There is a scoundrel who goes bowed down in black,
but inside he is full of deceit;

27he hangs his head and pretends not to hear,
but where he is not noticed he will get the better of you.

28If lack of strength keeps him from sinning,
when he finds an opportunity he will do harm.

29A man is known by his appearance,
and a sensible man is known by his face when you meet him.

30A man's clothing, and the laugh on his teeth,
and the way he walks show what he is.

  • v2 "Wine and women lead men of understanding astray" — the counsel of King Lemuel's mother, Do not give your strength to women (Reproof 7:3–4; Proverbs 31:3–4).

  • v5 "Whoever takes delight in his heart" — so Swete's Greek (kardia); the line reads more easily as "whoever takes delight in wickedness" (kakia).

  • vv7–12 — on gossip: Have you heard something? Let it die with you. The fool who hears a secret is in labor until he delivers it (v11).

  • vv13–17 "Question a friend… before you threaten him" — the command of Leviticus 19:17, You shall be sure to correct your neighbor; Jesus, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone (Matthew 18:15).

  • v16 "who has not sinned with his tongue?" — James 3:2, we all stumble in many ways; if anyone does not stumble in what he says, he is a perfect man.

  • vv18, 19, 21 — Swete's Greek gives these verse numbers and no words (see the note on 1:5).

  • vv26–27 "bowed down in black" — dressed and bent as a mourner, a show of grief over a heart of deceit; "pretends not to hear" — heterokōphōn, "deaf in one ear."

chapters.title: A Time to Keep Silent
chapters.html:
Sirach 20

1There is a reproof that is untimely,
and there is a man who keeps silent, and he is wise.

2How much better it is to reprove than to fume!
The one who confesses will be kept from loss.

3(This verse is not in the Greek text followed here; see the note.)

4Like a eunuch's desire to violate a girl
is the man who does justice by force.

5There is one who keeps silent and is found wise,
and another who is hated for his much talk.

6There is one who keeps silent because he has no answer,
and another who keeps silent because he knows the right time.

7A wise man will keep silent until the right time,
but a braggart and fool will let the time go by.

8Whoever uses many words will be abhorred,
and whoever takes authority upon himself will be hated.

9There is success that a man finds in misfortune,
and there is a windfall that turns into loss.

10There is a gift that will profit you nothing,
and there is a gift that brings a double return.

11There is loss because of glory,
and there is one who has lifted his head from humiliation.

12There is one who buys much for little,
and pays for it seven times over.

13The wise man makes himself loved by his words,
but the courtesies of fools are poured out for nothing.

14A fool's gift will profit you nothing,
for his eyes are many instead of one.

15He gives little and reproaches much,
and opens his mouth like a herald;
today he lends, and tomorrow he asks it back;
such a man is hateful.

16The fool says, "I have no friend,
and there is no thanks for my good deeds;
those who eat my bread have evil tongues."

17How often, and by how many, will he be laughed at!

18A slip on the pavement is better than a slip of the tongue;
so the fall of the wicked will come quickly.

19A graceless man is like a story told at the wrong time;
it will be always on the lips of the undisciplined.

20A proverb from a fool's lips will be rejected,
for he does not tell it at its proper time.

21There is one who is kept from sinning by his want,
and when he rests, his conscience does not trouble him.

22There is one who destroys his own soul through shame,
and destroys it out of regard for a fool.

23There is one who out of shame makes promises to a friend,
and gains him as an enemy for nothing.

24A lie is an ugly blemish on a man;
it will be always on the lips of the undisciplined.

25A thief is preferable to a habitual liar,
but both will inherit destruction.

26The way of a liar is disgrace,
and his shame is always with him.
Sayings in proverbs.

27The wise man will advance himself by his words,
and a sensible man will please great men.

28Whoever tills the soil will heap up his harvest,
and whoever pleases great men will win pardon for wrongdoing.

29Gifts and presents blind the eyes of the wise;
like a muzzle on the mouth they turn away reproofs.

30Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure —
what use is there in either?

31Better is a man who hides his folly
than a man who hides his wisdom.

Notes

  • v3 — Swete's Greek gives this verse number and no words (see the note on 1:5).

  • v4 "Like a eunuch's desire to violate a girl" — the desire that cannot be fulfilled, and is wrong besides: so is justice done by force. The picture returns in 30:20.

  • vv5–7 "There is one who keeps silent… because he knows the right time" — a time to keep silent, and a time to speak (Ecclesiastes 3:7); Even a fool who keeps silent is considered wise (Proverbs 17:28).

  • v14 "his eyes are many instead of one" — he gives one gift and looks for many in return.

  • v20 "A proverb from a fool's lips will be rejected" — Reproof 2:7 (Proverbs 26:7), Like the legs of the lame, which hang useless, is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

  • v26 "Sayings in proverbs." — a heading written into the Greek text, as at 18:30, over the sayings that follow.

  • v28 "will win pardon for wrongdoing" — exilasetai adikian, "will atone for wrong": the favor of the great covers a man's faults.

  • v29 "Gifts and presents blind the eyes of the wise" — the words of the Law, a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise (Deuteronomy 16:19).

  • vv30–31 "Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure" — compare the servant who hid his talent in the ground (Matthew 25:25).
